title.zh: 卷一百六十四 志第一百十七 職官四
title.raw: 卷一百六十四 志第一百十七 職官四 Volume 164 Treatises 117: Offical Posts 4

sentences.zh: 御史臺 秘書省 殿中省 太常寺 宗正寺 大宗正司附 光祿寺 衛尉寺 太僕寺

translations.literal: Censorate; Secretariat; Palace Domestic Service; Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Court of the Imperial Clan; Office of the Great Clan Patriarch attached; Court of Imperial Entertainments; Court of the Imperial Insignia; Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate; the Secretariat; the Palace Domestic Service; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; the Court of the Imperial Clan; the Office of the Great Clan Patriarch (attached); the Court of Imperial Entertainments; the Court of the Imperial Insignia; and the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 御史臺掌

translations.literal: The Censorate was charged with
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate was responsible for

sentences.zh: 糾察官邪，肅正綱紀。

translations.literal: investigating and exposing official wrongdoing and rectifying discipline and statutes.
translations.idiomatic: investigating official misconduct and upholding institutional discipline.

sentences.zh: 大事則廷辨，小事則奏彈。

translations.literal: Major matters were argued in court; minor matters were memorialized and impeached.
translations.idiomatic: Major cases were debated at court; lesser ones were reported and impeached by memorial.

sentences.zh: 其屬有三院：一曰臺院，侍御史隸焉 ；

translations.literal: Its subordinate offices comprised three bureaus: first, the Bureau of the Censorate, to which Attending Censors were attached;
translations.idiomatic: It had three bureaus: the Bureau of the Censorate, staffed by Attending Censors;

sentences.zh: 二曰殿院，殿中侍御史隸焉；

translations.literal: second, the Palace Bureau, to which Palace Attending Censors were attached;
translations.idiomatic: second, the Palace Bureau, staffed by Palace Attending Censors;

sentences.zh: 三曰察院，監察御史隸焉。

translations.literal: third, the Investigation Bureau, to which Investigating Censors were attached.
translations.idiomatic: and third, the Investigation Bureau, staffed by Investigating Censors.

sentences.zh: 凡祭祀、朝會，則率其屬正 百官之班序。

translations.literal: Whenever there were sacrifices or court assemblies, it led its subordinates to set in order the ranks of the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: At sacrifices and court assemblies, its officers led their staffs in arranging the order of ranks among all officials.

sentences.zh: 咸平四年，以御史二人充左右巡使；

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianping, two censors were appointed as Left and Right Touring Commissioners;
translations.idiomatic: In 1001, two censors were appointed Left and Right Touring Commissioners;

sentences.zh: 分糾不如法者。

translations.literal: they were to investigate separately those who did not conform to regulations.
translations.idiomatic: each to investigate officials who failed to observe protocol.

sentences.zh: 文官，右巡主之，武 官，左巡主之；

translations.literal: civil officials were supervised by the Right Tour; military officials, by the Left Tour;
translations.idiomatic: the Right Tour supervised civil officials and the Left Tour supervised military officials;

sentences.zh: 分其職掌，糾其違失，常參班簿、祿料、假告皆主之。

translations.literal: they divided their duties, investigated their violations, and had charge of attendance registers for regular court participants, salary allotments, and leave petitions.
translations.idiomatic: they divided responsibilities, investigated breaches, and oversaw attendance rolls, salary allotments, and leave requests for officials in regular court attendance.

sentences.zh: 祭祀則兼監祭使 ，掌受誓戒致齋，檢視糾劾。

translations.literal: at sacrifices they also served as Supervising Sacrifice Commissioners, receiving oaths and fasting, inspecting and impeaching.
translations.idiomatic: at sacrifices they also served as Supervising Sacrifice Commissioners, taking oaths, observing fasting, and inspecting and impeaching infractions.

sentences.zh: 又有廊下使，專掌入閤監食；

translations.literal: there were also Corridor Commissioners, who exclusively supervised food when entering the Inner Hall;
translations.idiomatic: there were also Corridor Commissioners, who supervised meals on entry to the Inner Hall;

sentences.zh: 又有監香使，掌國忌行香， 二使臨時充。

translations.literal: there were also Incense Supervising Commissioners, who managed state mourning incense offerings; the two commissioners were filled on a temporary basis.
translations.idiomatic: and Incense Supervising Commissioners, who oversaw state-mourning incense rites—these two posts were filled ad hoc.

sentences.zh: 通稱曰五使。

translations.literal: Collectively they were called the Five Commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Together they were known as the Five Commissioners.

sentences.zh: 元豐正官名，於是使名悉罷。

translations.literal: When the Yuanfeng regular official titles were instituted, all these commissioner titles were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuanfeng reforms established regular official titles, all these commissioner designations were abolished.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief

sentences.zh: 宋初不除正員，止為加官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Song, the regular post was not filled; it served only as an additional title.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song dynasty the regular post was not filled; the title was conferred only as an additional rank.

sentences.zh: 檢校官帶憲銜，有至檢校御史大夫者。

translations.literal: Acting officials bore censorate designations, some reaching Acting Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Acting officials could bear censorate titles, in some cases as high as Acting Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 元豐官制行，亦并除 去。

translations.literal: When the Yuanfeng official system was implemented, this too was abolished altogether.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuanfeng official system took effect, this title was abolished as well.

sentences.zh: 一人，為臺長，舊兼理檢使。

translations.literal: One post, as head of the Censorate; formerly also concurrently served as Investigating Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: One post, as head of the Censorate; formerly the incumbent also doubled as Investigating Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 凡除中丞而官未至者，皆除右諫議大夫權。

translations.literal: Whenever someone was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief but had not yet arrived to take office, he was all appointed Acting Right Remonstrance Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief who had not yet assumed the post was first named Acting Right Remonstrance Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 熙寧五年，以 知雜御史鄧綰為中丞，初除諫議大夫，王安石言礙近制，止以綰為龍圖閣待制權，御史 中丞不遷諫議大夫自綰始。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xining, Supervising Miscellaneous Affairs Censor Deng Wan was made Vice Censor-in-Chief; he was first appointed Remonstrance Grand Master, but Wang Anshi said this conflicted with recent regulations, so Wan was made only Acting Awaiting Compiler at the Dragon Diagram Hall; from Wan onward, the Vice Censor-in-Chief was no longer transferred through Remonstrance Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: In 1072, Supervising Miscellaneous Affairs Censor Deng Wan was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief. He was first named Remonstrance Grand Master, but Wang Anshi objected that this violated recent practice, and Wan received only Acting Awaiting Compiler at the Dragon Diagram Hall. From Wan onward, the Vice Censor-in-Chief was no longer routed through the Remonstrance Grand Master post.

sentences.zh: 九年，鄧潤甫自正言知制誥為中丞，以宰相屬官不可長憲府 ，於是復遷右諫議大夫權。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Deng Runfu went from Rectifier and Drafting Drafter to Vice Censor-in-Chief; because a chancellor's subordinate could not long head the Censorate, he was again transferred to Acting Right Remonstrance Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: In 1076, Deng Runfu moved from Rectifier and Drafting Drafter to Vice Censor-in-Chief. Because a chancellor's subordinate could not long head the censorate, he was again made Acting Right Remonstrance Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 元豐五年，以承議郎徐禧為知制誥權中丞。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanfeng, Gentleman for Discussion of Governance Xu Xi was made Drafting Drafter and Acting Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In 1082, Gentleman for Discussion of Governance Xu Xi was appointed Drafting Drafter and Acting Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 禧言：「中丞糾 彈之任，赴舍人院行詞，疑若未安。」

translations.literal: Xi said: "The Vice Censor-in-Chief's duty is impeachment; to go to the Academy of Scholars to draft edicts seems perhaps improper."
translations.idiomatic: Xi said, "The vice censor's role is impeachment; having to draft edicts at the Academy of Scholars seems ill suited to that office."

sentences.zh: 會官制行，罷知制誥職，乃以本官試中丞。

translations.literal: When the official system was implemented, the Drafting Drafter post was abolished, and he was then tried in his original rank as Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the new official system took effect, the drafting post was abolished, and he served as Vice Censor-in-Chief on probation in his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 南渡 初除官最多，隆興後被擢浸少。

translations.literal: After the southward relocation, appointments were most numerous at first; after Longxing, those promoted gradually became fewer.
translations.idiomatic: After the court moved south, appointments were most frequent at first; after the Longxing era, promotions to the post grew steadily rarer.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十年，始除黃洽，又三年再除蔣繼周。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chunxi, Huang Qia was first appointed; three years later Jiang Jizhou was again appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1183, Huang Qia received the first appointment in years; three years later Jiang Jizhou was appointed again.

sentences.zh: 臺諫例不兼 講讀，神宗命呂正獻，亦止命時赴講筵。

translations.literal: By precedent censorate and remonstrance officials did not concurrently serve as lecture readers; Emperor Shenzong ordered Lü the Upright Contributor, but only commanded him to attend the lecture hall at times.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, censors and remonstrators did not also serve as lecture readers. Emperor Shenzong appointed Lü Gongzhu to read, but only required him to attend lectures occasionally.

sentences.zh: 中興兼者二人，万俟离、羅汝楫皆以秦檜意。

translations.literal: After the restoration, two held concurrent posts: Moqi Xie and Luo Ruji, both by Qin Hui's intent.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration, only two held concurrent lecture posts—Moqi Xie and Luo Ruji—both at Qin Hui's behest.

sentences.zh: 慶元後，司諫以上無不預經筵者矣。

translations.literal: After Qingyuan, none from Supervising Censor upward failed to participate in the classics lecture.
translations.idiomatic: After the Qingyuan era, every official from Supervising Censor upward took part in the classics lecture.

sentences.zh: 侍御 史一人，掌貳臺政。

translations.literal: Attending Censor, one post, who assisted in censorate administration.
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor, one post, assisting in the administration of the censorate.

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史 二人，掌以儀法糾百官之失。

translations.literal: Palace Attending Censors, two posts, who by ritual regulations investigated the faults of the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attending Censors, two posts, responsible for investigating breaches of court ritual among all officials.

sentences.zh: 凡大朝會及朔望、六參，則東西對立，彈其失儀者。

translations.literal: Whenever there were great court assemblies and the new and full moons and the six regular audiences, they stood facing east and west and impeached those who breached ritual.
translations.idiomatic: At major assemblies and at the new- and full-moon audiences and the six regular sessions, they stood on east and west sides of the hall and impeached officials who breached protocol.

sentences.zh: 監察御史

translations.literal: Investigating Censor
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor

sentences.zh: 六人，掌分察六曹及百司之事，糾其謬誤，大事則奏劾，小事則舉正。

translations.literal: Six posts, who were charged with dividing supervision of the Six Ministries and the affairs of the hundred offices, investigating their errors; major matters were memorialized and impeached, minor matters were reported and corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Six posts, each supervising one of the Six Ministries and other agencies, investigating errors. Major cases were reported and impeached; minor ones were corrected on the spot.

sentences.zh: 迭監祠祭。

translations.literal: They took turns supervising sacrificial rites.
translations.idiomatic: They took turns supervising state sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 歲詣 三省、樞密院以下輪治。

translations.literal: Each year they went in rotation to the Three Departments, the Bureau of Military Affairs, and offices below.
translations.idiomatic: Each year they rotated through the Three Departments, the Bureau of Military Affairs, and subordinate offices.

sentences.zh: 凡六察之事，稽其多寡當否，歲終條具殿最，以詔黜陟。

translations.literal: For all matters of the Six Investigations, they examined whether quantities were appropriate, and at year's end listed grades of merit to inform dismissal and promotion.
translations.idiomatic: For the Six Investigations they audited whether workloads were appropriate, and at year's end submitted merit rankings to guide promotions and demotions.

sentences.zh: 百官 應赴臺參謝辭者，以拜跪、書札體驗其老疾。

translations.literal: For all officials who should come to the Censorate to pay respects or take leave, they tested age and illness by bowing and kneeling and by the style of written documents.
translations.idiomatic: For officials required to attend the censorate for farewells or thanks, they assessed age and infirmity by observing bows and kneels and by the form of written submissions.

sentences.zh: 凡事經郡縣、監司、省曹不能直者，直牒 閤門，上殿論奏。

translations.literal: Whenever a matter had passed through prefectures and counties, circuit supervisors, and ministry bureaus without being resolved, they sent a direct dispatch to the Gatekeepers' Office and ascended the hall to discuss and memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: Cases that prefectures, circuit supervisors, or ministry bureaus could not resolve were sent directly to the Gatekeepers' Office for audience and memorial at court.

sentences.zh: 官卑而入殿中監察御史者，謂之「裡行」。

translations.literal: Those of low rank who entered as Palace Investigating Censors were called "acting within."
translations.idiomatic: Lower-ranking appointees who served as investigating censors within the bureau were called "acting within" (lixing).

sentences.zh: 治平四年，中丞王陶言： 「奉詔舉臺官，而才行可舉者多以資淺不應格。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhiping, Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Tao said: "By imperial order I am to recommend censorate officials, yet those whose talent and conduct are recommendable are mostly disqualified for shallow seniority."
translations.idiomatic: In 1067, Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Tao said, "By edict I am to recommend censorate officials, yet many qualified candidates are rejected for insufficient seniority."

sentences.zh: 乃詔舉三任以上知縣為裡行。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered that magistrates of three or more terms be recommended as acting within.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered that magistrates who had served three or more terms could be recommended as acting within.

sentences.zh: 熙寧二 年詔：「御史闕，委中丞奏舉，毋拘官職高下兼權。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Xining an edict said: "When censor posts are vacant, the Vice Censor-in-Chief is to memorialize recommendations, without restriction as to high or low office or concurrent acting appointment."
translations.idiomatic: In 1069 an edict said, "When censor posts are vacant, the vice censor shall recommend candidates without regard to rank or acting appointment."

sentences.zh: 三年，孫覺薦秀州軍事推官李定 ，對稱旨，為太子中允權監察御史裡行，由選人為御史自定始。

translations.literal: In the third year, Sun Jue recommended Xiuzhou Military Push Officer Li Ding; in audience he pleased the emperor and was made Acting Palace Investigating Censor within as Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent; from Ding began the selection of censors from examination appointees.
translations.idiomatic: In 1070, Sun Jue recommended Li Ding, military push officer of Xiuzhou. Ding pleased the emperor in audience and was named Acting Investigating Censor within as Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent—the first time an examination appointee became a censor.

sentences.zh: 於是知制誥宋敏求、蘇 頌、李大臨以定資淺，封還詞頭，不草制，相繼罷去。

translations.literal: Thereupon Drafting Drafters Song Minqiu, Su Song, and Li Daling, on the ground that Ding's seniority was shallow, sealed and returned the drafting headers, refused to draft the appointment, and were dismissed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting drafters Song Minqiu, Su Song, and Li Daling then sealed and returned the appointment draft, refusing to write it on grounds of Ding's low seniority, and were dismissed one after another.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，監察御史胡舜陟言：「監察御史自唐至本朝，皆論政事、擊官邪，元豐、紹 聖著於甲令，崇寧大臣欲其便己，遂更成憲。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang, Investigating Censor Hu Shunzhi said: "From Tang to our dynasty, Investigating Censors have all discussed state affairs and attacked official wickedness; Yuanfeng and Shaosheng inscribed this in statutory orders, but in Chongning grand ministers wished them convenient to themselves and thus changed it into permanent regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In 1126, Investigating Censor Hu Shunzhi said, "From Tang through our dynasty, investigating censors have debated policy and attacked corrupt officials—rules Yuanfeng and Shaosheng put in statute. Chongning ministers changed the rules to suit themselves.

sentences.zh: 乞令本臺增入監察御史言事之文。」

translations.literal: I beg that this bureau add back the text on Investigating Censors' right to speak on affairs."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that this bureau restore the investigating censors' authority to speak on affairs."

sentences.zh: 詔依 祖宗法。

translations.literal: An edict followed the ancestral regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered a return to ancestral practice.

sentences.zh: 又詔宰執不得薦舉臺諫官。

translations.literal: It was also decreed that chief ministers must not recommend censorate and remonstrance officials.
translations.idiomatic: The court also forbade chief ministers to recommend censorate and remonstrance officials.

sentences.zh: 舊臺令，御史上下半年分詣三省、樞密院點檢諸房 文字，輪詣尚書六曹按察；

translations.literal: By old censorate regulations, censors in the first and second halves of the year separately went to the Three Departments and the Bureau of Military Affairs to inspect documents in the various bureaus, and in rotation went to the Six Ministries of the Department of State Affairs to investigate;
translations.idiomatic: Under former censorate rules, censors in each half of the year inspected documents at the Three Departments and Bureau of Military Affairs and rotated through the Six Ministries of the Department of State Affairs;

sentences.zh: 奉行稽違，付受差失，咸得彈糾。

translations.literal: delays in carrying out orders, errors in transmission and receipt—all could be impeached.
translations.idiomatic: delays in execution, transmission errors, and similar faults were all subject to impeachment.

sentences.zh: 渡江後，稍闊不舉。

translations.literal: After crossing the Yangzi, this was gradually neglected and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: After the court crossed the Yangzi, these duties were gradually neglected.

sentences.zh: 紹興 三年，始復其舊。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shaoxing, the former practice was first restored.
translations.idiomatic: In 1133 the former practice was restored.

sentences.zh: 是年十一月，殿中侍御史常同言：「元豐始置六察，上自諸部、寺監 ，下至廩庫、場務，無不分隸，以詔廢置。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year, Palace Attending Censor Chang Tong said: "Yuanfeng first established the Six Investigations; from ministries and directorates above down to granaries and market offices below, none were not assigned in division, so that abolition and establishment might be by edict.
translations.idiomatic: That November, Palace Attending Censor Chang Tong said, "Yuanfeng created the Six Investigations so that every agency from ministries down to granaries and market offices fell under censorial oversight, with abolition and establishment subject to imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 而乃有寅緣申請，乞不隸臺察者，恐非法意 ，宜遵舊制。」

translations.literal: Yet there are those who by currying favor petition to be removed from censorate investigation—this perhaps is not the intent of the law; the old system should be followed."
translations.idiomatic: Yet some now petition by favor to escape censorial oversight—likely contrary to the law's intent. The old system should be followed."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 乾道二年詔：「自今非曾經兩任縣令，不得除監察御史。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiandao an edict said: "From now on, unless one has served two terms as county magistrate, one may not be appointed Investigating Censor."
translations.idiomatic: In 1166 an edict said, "Henceforth no one may be appointed investigating censor without having served two terms as county magistrate."

sentences.zh: 慶元 二年，侍御史黃黼言：「監察御史高宗時嘗置六員，孝宗時置三員，今分按之任止二人 ，乞增置一員。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Qingyuan, Attending Censor Huang Fu said: "Under Gaozong there were once six Investigating Censors; under Xiaozong three; now for divided investigation duties there are only two—I beg that one more post be added."
translations.idiomatic: In 1196, Attending Censor Huang Fu said, "Gaozong once appointed six investigating censors and Xiaozong three; today only two cover divided duties. I ask that one more post be added."

sentences.zh: 自後常置三員。

translations.literal: Thereafter three posts were regularly established.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter three posts were regularly maintained.

sentences.zh: 三京留司御史臺

translations.literal: Censorate of the Three Capitals on Detached Duty
translations.idiomatic: Censorate of the Three Capitals on Detached Duty

sentences.zh: 管勾臺事各一人，

translations.literal: Overseer of Bureau Affairs, one for each,
translations.idiomatic: Overseer of Bureau Affairs, one for each capital,

sentences.zh: （舊曰判臺。）〉

translations.literal: (Formerly called Director of the Bureau.)
translations.idiomatic: (formerly called Director of the Bureau.)

sentences.zh: 以朝官以上充。

translations.literal: filled by court officials of the fifth rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: filled by court officials of fifth rank and above.

sentences.zh: 掌拜表行香，糾舉違失。

translations.literal: They managed presenting memorials and offering incense, and investigated and reported violations.
translations.idiomatic: They oversaw presenting memorials and incense offerings and investigated breaches of protocol.

sentences.zh: 令史二人， 知班、驅使倌、書吏各一人，中興以後不置。

translations.literal: Clerks, two; Masters of Order, Attendants, and Copyists, one each—these were not established after the restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Two clerks, plus one Master of Order, one attendant, and one copyist each—these posts were not filled after the restoration.

sentences.zh: 秘書省 監 少監

translations.literal: Secretariat; Director; Vice Director
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat; Director; Vice Director

sentences.zh: 丞各一人，監掌古今經籍圖書、國史實錄、天文曆數之事，少監為之貳，而丞參領之。

translations.literal: Assistant Directors, one each; the Director managed ancient and modern classics, books, maps, the national history, veritable records, astronomy, and calendrical reckoning; the Vice Director was second to him, and the Assistant Directors shared in leading.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Directors, one each. The Director oversaw classics, books, maps, the national history, veritable records, astronomy, and calendrical matters; the Vice Director assisted, and the Assistant Directors shared administrative duties.

sentences.zh: 其屬有五：著作郎一人，著作佐郎二人，掌修纂日曆；

translations.literal: Its subordinates numbered five: Compiler, one; Assistant Compilers, two, who managed compilation of the calendar;
translations.idiomatic: It had five subordinate posts: one Compiler and two Assistant Compilers, who compiled the court calendar;

sentences.zh: 秘書郎二人，掌集賢院、史館、 昭文館、秘閣圖籍，以甲、乙、丙、丁為部，各分其類；

translations.literal: Secretariat Gentlemen, two, who managed the collections of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, the History Office, the Hall of Broad Learning, and the Secret Depository, using jia, yi, bing, and ding as sections, each dividing its categories;
translations.idiomatic: two Secretariat Gentlemen, who managed collections at the Hall of Gathered Worthies, History Office, Hall of Broad Learning, and Secret Depository, divided into jia, yi, bing, and ding sections by category;

sentences.zh: 校書郎四人，正字二人，掌校 讎典籍，判正訛謬，各以其職隸於長貳。

translations.literal: Collators, four; Rectifiers, two, who managed collation of classics, judging and correcting errors, each according to his office subordinate to the chief and second.
translations.idiomatic: four Collators and two Rectifiers, who collated texts and corrected errors, each reporting to the Director and Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 惟日曆非編修官不預。

translations.literal: Only for the calendar were those who were not compilation officials not permitted to participate.
translations.idiomatic: Only compilation officials could work on the calendar.

sentences.zh: 歲於仲夏曝書，則給酒 食費，尚書、學士、侍郎、待制、兩省諫官、御史並赴。

translations.literal: Each year in midsummer books were aired in the sun, and wine and food expenses were provided; Ministers, Academicians, Vice Ministers, Awaiting Compilers, remonstrance officials of the two departments, and censors all attended.
translations.idiomatic: Each midsummer the library aired its books and provided food and wine; ministers, academicians, vice ministers, awaiting compilers, remonstrators, and censors all attended.

sentences.zh: 遇庚伏，則前期遣中使諭旨， 聽以早歸。

translations.literal: When the geng dog-days occurred, beforehand a palace envoy was sent to convey the imperial will, permitting early departure.
translations.idiomatic: During the dog-days of summer, an imperial envoy announced beforehand that attendees might leave early.

sentences.zh: 大典禮，則長貳預集議。

translations.literal: For great ritual ceremonies, the chief and second participated in assembled deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: For major state rituals, the Director and Vice Director joined deliberations.

sentences.zh: 所以待遇儒臣，非他司比。

translations.literal: Thus were scholar-officials treated—unlike any other agency.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the treatment accorded scholar-officials—unmatched by any other agency.

sentences.zh: 宴設錫予，率循故事。

translations.literal: Banquets, provisions, and bestowals all followed established precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Banquets, provisions, and imperial gifts followed long-established precedent.

sentences.zh: 宋初，置三館長慶門北，謂之西館。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Song, the Three Halls were placed north of the Changqing Gate, called the Western Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song, the Three Halls were established north of the Changqing Gate and called the Western Hall.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，於昇龍門東北，創立三館書院。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo, northeast of the Ascending Dragon Gate, the Three Halls Academy was newly established.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Taiping Xingguo era, the Three Halls Academy was founded northeast of the Ascending Dragon Gate.

sentences.zh: 三年 ，賜名崇文院，遷西館書貯焉。

translations.literal: In the third year it was granted the name Hall of Esteeming Literature, and the books of the Western Hall were moved and stored there.
translations.idiomatic: In 978 it was named the Hall of Esteeming Literature, and the Western Hall's collections were moved there.

sentences.zh: 東廊為集賢書庫，西廊分四部，為史館書庫。

translations.literal: The east corridor was the book depository of the Hall of Gathered Worthies; the west corridor was divided into four sections as the book depository of the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: The east corridor housed the Hall of Gathered Worthies library; the west corridor, divided into four sections, housed the History Office library.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符 八年，創外院於右掖門外。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, an outer court was created outside the Right Flank Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1015 an outer compound was built outside the Right Flank Gate.

sentences.zh: 天禧初，令以三館為額，置檢討、校勘等員。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxi, it was ordered that the Three Halls be taken as the title, and Investigating and Collating posts and the like were established.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianxi era, the Three Halls were formally titled and Investigating and Collating posts were established.

sentences.zh: 檢討以京朝官 充，校勘自京朝、幕職至選人皆得備選。

translations.literal: Investigating posts were filled by capital court officials; collating posts could be selected from capital court officials, staff appointees, down to examination appointees.
translations.idiomatic: Investigators were drawn from capital court officials; collators could be court officials, staff appointees, or examination appointees.

sentences.zh: 以內侍二人為勾當官，通掌三館圖籍事，孔目 官、表奏官、掌捨各一人。

translations.literal: Two inner attendants served as Supervisory Officials, jointly managing the maps and books of the Three Halls; one Clerk, one Memorial Presentation Officer, and one Keeper of Quarters each.
translations.idiomatic: Two palace eunuchs served as supervisory officials over the Three Halls collections, with one clerk, one memorial presenter, and one quarters keeper each.

sentences.zh: 又有監書庫內侍一人。

translations.literal: There was also one inner attendant supervising the book depository.
translations.idiomatic: One eunuch also supervised the book depository.

sentences.zh: 兼監秘閣圖籍孔目官一人。

translations.literal: One Clerk concurrently supervising the maps and books of the Secret Depository.
translations.idiomatic: One clerk also supervised the Secret Depository collections.

sentences.zh: 係端拱元年就崇文院中堂建閤，以三館書籍真本並內出古畫墨跡等藏之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Duan Gong a pavilion was built in the central hall of the Hall of Esteeming Literature, storing authentic books of the Three Halls together with ancient paintings and ink traces issued from within.
translations.idiomatic: In 988 a pavilion was built in the central hall of the Hall of Esteeming Literature to store authentic Three Halls texts and imperial paintings and calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 淳化元年，詔 次三館置直閤、

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunhua, an edict ordered that below the Three Halls there be established Attendants of the Pavilion,
translations.idiomatic: In 990 an edict ordered Attendants of the Pavilion established under the Three Halls,

sentences.zh: （以朝官充。）〉

translations.literal: (filled by court officials.)
translations.idiomatic: (filled by court officials.)

sentences.zh: 校理，

translations.literal: Collators,
translations.idiomatic: Collators,

sentences.zh: （以京朝官充。）〉

translations.literal: (filled by capital court officials.)
translations.idiomatic: (filled by capital court officials.)

sentences.zh: 以諸司三品、兩省五品以上官 一人判閤事。

translations.literal: one official of third rank in the various bureaus or fifth rank and above in the two departments to direct pavilion affairs.
translations.idiomatic: with one third-rank bureau official or fifth-rank official of the two departments to direct pavilion affairs.

sentences.zh: 直閤、校理通掌閤事，掌繕寫秘閣所藏。

translations.literal: Attendants of the Pavilion and Collators jointly managed pavilion affairs and managed copying what the Secret Depository stored.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants and Collators jointly managed the pavilion and copied works held in the Secret Depository.

sentences.zh: 供御人、裝裁匠十二人。

translations.literal: Provisioners for the imperial household and book-binding craftsmen, twelve persons.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve provisioners for the imperial household and book-binding craftsmen.

sentences.zh: 元豐五 年，職事官貼職悉罷，以崇文院為秘書省官屬，始立為定員，分案四，置吏八。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanfeng, all supplemental posts for regular-duty officials were abolished; the Hall of Esteeming Literature was made subordinate to the Secretariat; fixed quotas were first established, with four sections and eight clerks.
translations.idiomatic: In 1082 all supplemental posts for regular-duty officials were abolished, the Hall of Esteeming Literature was subordinated to the Secretariat, fixed quotas were established for the first time, with four sections and eight clerks.

sentences.zh: （崇文 院，太平興國三年置。

translations.literal: (The Hall of Esteeming Literature was established in the third year of Taiping Xingguo.
translations.idiomatic: (The Hall of Esteeming Literature was established in 978.

sentences.zh: 端拱元年，建秘閣於院中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Duan Gong, the Secret Depository was built within the hall.
translations.idiomatic: In 988 the Secret Depository was built within the hall.

sentences.zh: 昭文館、史館、集賢院皆沿唐制立名 ，但有書庫寓於崇文院廡下。

translations.literal: The Hall of Broad Learning, History Office, and Hall of Gathered Worthies all retained Tang-era names, but only had book depositories lodged under the side halls of the Hall of Esteeming Literature.
translations.idiomatic: The Hall of Broad Learning, History Office, and Hall of Gathered Worthies kept their Tang-era titles, but their book depositories were housed in the side halls of the Hall of Esteeming Literature.

sentences.zh: 三館、秘閣、崇文院各置貼職官。

translations.literal: The Three Halls, Secret Depository, and Hall of Esteeming Literature each had supplemental appointment officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Halls, Secret Depository, and Hall of Esteeming Literature each had supplemental appointment officials.

sentences.zh: 又有集賢殿修撰、直龍 圖閣、校勘，通謂之館職。

translations.literal: There were also Hall Compilers of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, Direct Attendants of the Dragon Diagram Hall, and Collators—collectively called hall appointments.
translations.idiomatic: There were also Hall Compilers, Direct Attendants of the Dragon Diagram Hall, and Collators—collectively called hall appointments.

sentences.zh: 初，英宗謂輔臣曰：「館閣所以育雋材，比選數人出使，無 可者，豈乏材耶？」

translations.literal: At first Emperor Yingzong said to his chief ministers: "The halls and pavilion exist to nurture outstanding talent. Several persons were lately selected for missions abroad, yet none were suitable—is talent truly lacking?"
translations.idiomatic: Early on Emperor Yingzong told his chief ministers: "The halls and pavilion exist to nurture outstanding talent. Several men were recently chosen for foreign missions, yet none were fit—are we truly short of talent?"

sentences.zh: 歐陽脩曰：「今取材路狹，館閣止用選人編校書籍，故進用稍遲。」

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu said: "The path for selecting talent is now narrow. The halls and pavilion employ only examination appointees to edit and collate books, so advancement is somewhat delayed."
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu replied: "The avenues for selecting talent have narrowed. The halls and pavilion use only examination appointees to edit and collate books, so promotion comes slowly."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿等各舉數人，雖親戚世家勿避。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Each of you recommend several persons; do not avoid relatives of eminent families."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Each of you recommend several men—do not shrink from relatives of eminent families."

sentences.zh: 於是宰相琦、公亮，參知政事修、概各薦 五人，未及試，神宗登極，先召十人試以詩賦，而開封府界提點陳汝義別以奏封稱旨預 試。

translations.literal: Thereupon the chief councillors Qi and Gongliang and Associate Administrators of Affairs Xiu and Gai each recommended five persons. Before they could be tested, Shenzong ascended the throne and first summoned ten persons to be tested with regulated verse and fu; separately, Chen Ruyi, Supervisor of the Kaifeng Metropolitan Boundary, submitted a memorial that pleased the throne and he was included in the test in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Chief Councillors Qi and Gongliang and Associate Administrators Xiu and Gai each recommended five men. Before they could be examined, Shenzong took the throne and first summoned ten candidates to be tested in regulated verse and fu; separately, Chen Ruyi, supervisor of the Kaifeng metropolitan boundary, won advance inclusion in the examination with a memorial that pleased the throne.

sentences.zh: 於是御史吳申言：「試館職者請策以經史及世務，毋用辭賦。」

translations.literal: Thereupon Investigating Censor Wu Shen said: "Those tested for hall appointments should be examined by policy questions on the classics, histories, and current affairs—do not use belletristic composition."
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Wu Shen then urged: "Candidates for hall appointments should be tested on the classics, histories, and current affairs by policy questions—not belles-lettres."

sentences.zh: 遂詔：「自今試館 職專用策論。」

translations.literal: An edict followed: "Henceforth testing for hall appointments shall use policy discourse exclusively."
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: "Henceforth hall appointment examinations shall use policy discourse only."

sentences.zh: 熙寧二年，置崇文校書，始除河南府永安主簿邢恕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xi Ning, the post of Collator of the Hall of Esteeming Literature was established; the first appointment went to Xing Shu, Registrar of Yong'an in Henan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1069 the post of Collator of the Hall of Esteeming Literature was established; the first appointee was Xing Shu, registrar of Yong'an in Henan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 乃詔自今應選舉可 用人併除校書，候二年取旨除館職官。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered that from now on all who were usable from the examinations should concurrently be appointed Collators; after two years, by imperial order they would receive hall appointment posts.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered that henceforth all examination candidates deemed fit should be appointed Collators concurrently; after two years they would receive hall appointment posts by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 五年，以隸秘書省。）〉

translations.literal: In the fifth year it was subordinated to the Secretariat.)
translations.idiomatic: In 1082 it was subordinated to the Secretariat.)

sentences.zh: 元祐初，復置直集賢院、校理。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou, Direct Attendants of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and Collators were reestablished.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yuanyou era, Direct Attendants of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and Collators were reestablished.

sentences.zh: 自校理而上，職有六等，內外官並許帶，恩數仍舊。

translations.literal: From Collator upward there were six ranks of posts; both inner and outer officials were permitted to hold them concurrently, with perquisites unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: From Collator upward there were six ranks; both capital and local officials could hold them concurrently, with perquisites unchanged.

sentences.zh: 又 立試中人館職法，選人除正字，京官除校書郎。

translations.literal: Regulations for those who passed the examination to enter hall appointments were also established: examination appointees received Rectifier posts; capital officials received Collator posts.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations were also set for examination entrants to hall appointments: examination appointees were made Rectifiers; capital officials were made Collators.

sentences.zh: （校書郎供職二年，除集賢校理。

translations.literal: (After two years of service as Collator, one was appointed Collator of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: (After two years as Collator, one was appointed Collator of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.

sentences.zh: 秘書 郎、著作佐郎比集賢校理。

translations.literal: Secretariat Gentlemen and Assistant Compilers were equivalent to Collators of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Gentlemen and Assistant Compilers ranked with Collators of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.

sentences.zh: 著作郎比直集賢院、直秘閣。

translations.literal: Compilers were equivalent to Direct Attendants of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and the Secret Depository.
translations.idiomatic: Compilers ranked with Direct Attendants of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and the Secret Depository.

sentences.zh: 丞及三年除秘閣校理。）〉

translations.literal: After three years as Assistant Director, one was appointed Collator of the Secret Depository.)
translations.idiomatic: After three years as Assistant Director, one was appointed Collator of the Secret Depository.)

sentences.zh: 三年 二月，詔御試唱名日，秘書丞至正字升殿侍立。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year, an edict ordered that on the day palace examination names were called, Secretariat Assistant Directors through Rectifiers should ascend the hall and stand in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year, an edict ordered that on palace examination day, Secretariat Assistant Directors through Rectifiers should ascend the hall and stand in attendance.

sentences.zh: 九月，覆試賢良於閤下。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, worthy and able men were retested beneath the Retiring Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month worthy and able candidates were retested beneath the Retiring Hall.

sentences.zh: 五年，置集賢 院學士并校對黃本書籍官員。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Academicians of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and officials collating imperial yellow-skin books were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Academicians of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and officials to collate imperial yellow-skin editions were established.

sentences.zh: （紹聖初，罷校對，以編修日曆選本省，易集賢院學士為 殿修撰，直院為直秘閣，集賢校理為秘書校理。）〉

translations.literal: (At the beginning of Shaosheng, collators were abolished and selection for compiling the calendar was shifted to this province; Hall of Gathered Worthies Academicians were changed to Hall Compilers, Direct Attendants of the Hall to Direct Attendants of the Secret Depository, and Collators of the Hall of Gathered Worthies to Secretariat Collators.)
translations.idiomatic: (At the start of Shaosheng, collators were abolished and calendar compilation was staffed from the Secretariat; Hall Academicians became Hall Compilers, Direct Attendants of the Hall became Direct Attendants of the Secret Depository, and Hall Collators became Secretariat Collators.)

sentences.zh: 十二月，詔禮部，本省長貳定校讎之 課，月終具奏。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the Ministry of Rites was ordered: the chief and second of this province were to fix collation quotas and submit a memorial each month-end.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Ministry of Rites was instructed: the Secretariat Director and Vice Director were to set collation quotas and report monthly.

sentences.zh: （入伏午時減半，過渡伏依舊，從蘇軾之請。）〉

translations.literal: (Work was halved at the noon hour during dog-days; after the transitional dog-days it reverted to the old practice, at Su Shi's request.)
translations.idiomatic: (Work hours at noon were halved during dog-days; after the transitional dog-days the old schedule resumed, at Su Shi's request.)

sentences.zh: 又罷本省官任滿除館職 法。

translations.literal: The regulation whereby provincial officials upon completion of term received hall appointments was also abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The rule granting hall appointments to Secretariat officials upon completing their terms was also abolished.

sentences.zh: 元符二年，詔職事官罷帶館職，悉復元豐官制。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanfu, regular-duty officials were ordered to cease holding hall appointments concurrently; the Yuanfeng official system was fully restored.
translations.idiomatic: In 1099 regular-duty officials were ordered to cease holding hall appointments concurrently, and the Yuanfeng official system was fully restored.

sentences.zh: 崇寧五年，詔館閣併除進士出身人 。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chongning, an edict ordered that hall and pavilion appointments be given concurrently to jinshi degree holders.
translations.idiomatic: In 1106 an edict ordered that hall and pavilion appointments be granted concurrently to jinshi degree holders.

sentences.zh: 政和五年四月，詔秘書省殿以右文為名，改集賢殿修撰為右文殿修撰。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year of Zhenghe, an edict ordered that halls of the Secretariat be named for upholding letters; Hall Compilers of the Hall of Gathered Worthies were renamed Right-Letters Hall Compilers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of 1115 an edict ordered Secretariat halls renamed for upholding letters; Hall Compilers of the Hall of Gathered Worthies became Right-Letters Hall Compilers.

sentences.zh: 是月，駕詣景 靈宮朝獻，還幸秘書省。

translations.literal: That month the emperor proceeded to the Jingling Palace for the morning offering, then visited the Secretariat on the return.
translations.idiomatic: That month the emperor went to the Jingling Palace for the morning offering, then visited the Secretariat on his return.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「延見多士，歷覽藏書之府，祖宗遺文在焉，屋室淺狹 ，甚非稱太平右文之盛，宜重行修展。」

translations.literal: The edict said: "To meet many scholar-officials and tour the repository of books—there lie the literary legacies of forefathers; the buildings are shallow and cramped, quite unworthy of the flourishing age of upholding letters on the right; they should be rebuilt and expanded afresh."
translations.idiomatic: The edict said: "To receive many scholars and tour the book repository where our forefathers' writings are kept—the buildings are cramped and unworthy of an age that esteems letters; they should be rebuilt and enlarged."

sentences.zh: 八月，詔秘書省移於新左藏庫，以其地為堂。

translations.literal: In the eighth month an edict ordered the Secretariat moved to the new Left Treasury and its former site made the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Secretariat was ordered moved to the new Left Treasury; its former site became the main hall.

sentences.zh: 七年，詔類集所訪遺書，名曰秘書總目。

translations.literal: In the seventh year an edict ordered classified compilation of books sought out, entitled General Catalogue of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year an edict ordered a classified catalogue of books collected, entitled the General Catalogue of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 宣和二年，立定秘書省員額：監、少監、丞並 依元豐舊制，著作郎以四員為額，校書郎二員，正字四員。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuanhe, fixed Secretariat quotas were established: Director, Vice Director, and Assistant Director all followed the Yuanfeng old system; Compilers were fixed at four, Collators at two, and Rectifiers at four.
translations.idiomatic: In 1120 fixed Secretariat quotas were set: Director, Vice Director, and Assistant Director followed the Yuanfeng system; Compilers were fixed at four, Collators at two, and Rectifiers at four.

sentences.zh: 渡江後，製作未遑。

translations.literal: After crossing the Yangtze, institutions could not yet be fully ordered.
translations.idiomatic: After the crossing of the Yangtze, institutions could not yet be fully restored.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，始詔置秘書省，權以秘監或少監一員，丞、著作郎佐各 一員，校書、正字各二員為額。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing, the Secretariat was first ordered established provisionally, with one Director or Vice Director, one each of Assistant Director, Compiler, and Assistant Compiler, and two each of Collator and Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: In 1131 the Secretariat was first ordered reestablished provisionally: one Director or Vice Director, one each of Assistant Director, Compiler, and Assistant Compiler, and two each of Collator and Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 續又參酌舊制，校書郎、正字召試學士院而後命之。

translations.literal: Thereafter the old system was consulted: Collators and Rectifiers were summoned for examination at the Academy before appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, following precedent, Collators and Rectifiers were examined at the Hanlin Academy before appointment.

sentences.zh: 自 是采求闕文，補綴漏逸，四庫書略備。

translations.literal: From then on lost texts were sought and gaps filled; the four depositories were roughly complete.
translations.idiomatic: From then on missing texts were sought and gaps filled; the four depositories were roughly restored.

sentences.zh: 即秘書省復建史館，以修神宗、哲宗實錄，選本 省官兼檢討、校勘，以侍從官充修撰。

translations.literal: The Secretariat then rebuilt the History Office to compile the Veritable Records of Shenzong and Zhezong; provincial officials were chosen concurrently as Investigators and Collators, and palace attendees served as Compilers.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat then rebuilt the History Office to compile the Veritable Records of Shenzong and Zhezong; its own officials served concurrently as investigators and collators, and palace attendees as compilers.

sentences.zh: 五年，效唐人十八學士之制，監、少、丞外，置 著作郎佐、秘書郎各二人，校書郎、正字通十二人。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, following the Tang custom of the Eighteen Academicians, beyond Director, Vice Director, and Assistant Director there were two each of Compilers, Assistant Compilers, and Secretariat Gentlemen, and twelve Collators and Rectifiers together.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, following the Tang model of the Eighteen Academicians, beyond Director, Vice Director, and Assistant Director there were two each of Compilers, Assistant Compilers, and Secretariat Gentlemen, and twelve Collators and Rectifiers in all.

sentences.zh: 又移史館於省之側，別為一所，以 增重其事。

translations.literal: The History Office was also moved beside the province as a separate establishment to give added weight to the work.
translations.idiomatic: The History Office was also moved beside the Secretariat as a separate compound to lend the work greater weight.

sentences.zh: 九年，詔著作局惟修日曆，遇修國史則開國史院，遇修實錄則開實錄院，以 正名實。

translations.literal: In the ninth year an edict ordered the Compilation Bureau to compile only the calendar; when compiling national history the National History Office was opened, and when compiling veritable records the Veritable Records Office was opened, to set names and realities aright.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year an edict ordered the Compilation Bureau to compile only the court calendar; when national history was compiled the National History Office opened, and when veritable records were compiled the Veritable Records Office opened—to align titles with duties.

sentences.zh: 十三年，詔復每歲曝書會。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year an edict restored the annual book-airing assembly.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the annual book-airing assembly was restored.

sentences.zh: 是冬，新省成，少監遊操援政和故事，乞置提舉官 ，遂以授禮部侍郎秦熹，令掌求遺書，仍鑄印以賜。

translations.literal: That winter, when the new provincial compound was completed, Vice Director You Cao cited the Zhenghe precedent and requested supervisory officials; therefore the post was given to Vice Minister of Rites Qin Xi, charging him to seek out lost books, and a seal was cast and bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when the new compound was completed, Vice Director You Cao cited the Zhenghe precedent and requested a supervisory official; the post went to Vice Minister of Rites Qin Xi, charged to seek lost books, and a seal was cast and bestowed.

sentences.zh: 置編定書籍官二人，以校書郎、正 字充。

translations.literal: Two officials for compiling and fixing books were established, filled by Collators and Rectifiers.
translations.idiomatic: Two book-compilation officials were established, filled by Collators and Rectifiers.

sentences.zh: 孝宗即位，詔館職儲養人才，不可定員。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong took the throne, an edict stated that hall appointments nurtured talent and should not have fixed quotas.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong took the throne, an edict declared that hall appointments existed to nurture talent and should not have fixed quotas.

sentences.zh: 幹道九年，正字止六員；

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Qiandao, Rectifiers were limited to six posts;
translations.idiomatic: In 1173 Rectifiers were limited to six posts;

sentences.zh: 淳熙二年，監、少並 置，皆前所未有。

translations.literal: in the second year of Chunxi, both Director and Vice Director were staffed—all unprecedented.
translations.idiomatic: in 1175 both Director and Vice Director were staffed for the first time.

sentences.zh: 除少監、丞外，以七員為額，尋復詔不立額。

translations.literal: Except for Vice Director and Assistant Director, a quota of seven was set, but soon an edict again ordered that no quota be fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from Vice Director and Assistant Director, a quota of seven was set, but soon an edict again abolished fixed quotas.

sentences.zh: 紹熙二年，館職闕人， 上令召試二員，謹加審擇，取學問議論平正之人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxi, with hall posts vacant, the emperor ordered two persons summoned for examination, to be chosen with care—men of learning whose discourse was balanced and correct.
translations.idiomatic: In 1191, with hall posts vacant, the emperor ordered two candidates summoned for examination, to be chosen carefully—men of learning whose views were sound and balanced.

sentences.zh: 自是，監、少、丞外，多止除二員， 是時，陳傅良上言：「請以右文、秘閣修撰并舊館閣校勘三等為史官。

translations.literal: Thereafter, beyond Director, Vice Director, and Assistant Director, mostly only two persons were appointed. At the time Chen Fuliang memorialized: "Please take Right-Letters compilers, Secret Depository compilers, and the former three ranks of hall collators as history officials.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, apart from Director, Vice Director, and Assistant Director, usually only two appointments were made. At the time Chen Fuliang urged: "Let Right-Letters compilers, Secret Depository compilers, and the former three ranks of hall collators serve as history officials.

sentences.zh: 自校勘供職，稍 遷秘閣修撰，又遷右文。

translations.literal: Beginning as collators, after a time promoted to Secret Depository Compiler, then to Right-Letters.
translations.idiomatic: They would begin as collators, advance to Secret Depository Compiler, then to Right-Letters Compiler.

sentences.zh: 在院三五年，如有勞績，就遷次對，庶幾有專官之效，無冷局 之嫌。」

translations.literal: After three to five years in the office, if there were meritorious service, advancement would follow in due course—thus there would be the effect of dedicated posts without the stigma of a cold bureau."
translations.idiomatic: After three to five years in office, those with merit would advance in turn—thus dedicated posts would have effect, without the stigma of a neglected bureau."

sentences.zh: 時論韙之，然不果行。

translations.literal: Opinion at the time approved, yet it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion approved, but the proposal was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 中興分案四：曰經籍，曰祝版，曰知雜，曰太史。

translations.literal: After the restoration four sections were established: Classics, Prayer Tablets, General Affairs, and Grand Astrologer.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration four sections were established: Classics, Prayer Tablets, General Affairs, and Grand Astrologer.

sentences.zh: 吏額 ：都、副孔目官二人，四庫書直官二人，表奏官、書庫官各一人，守當官二人，正名楷 書五人，守闕一人，正貼司及守闕各六人，監門官一人以武臣充，專知官一人。

translations.literal: Clerk quotas: Chief and Deputy Clerks, two; Four-Depository Book Attendants, two; Memorial Submission Clerk and Book Depository Clerk, one each; Custodial Clerks, two; Regular Clerks for fair-copy, five; Acting Clerk, one; Regular Petition Clerks and Acting Clerks, six each; Gate Supervisory Official, one filled by a military official; Dedicated Custodian, one.
translations.idiomatic: Clerk quotas: two chief and deputy clerks; two four-depository book attendants; one memorial submission clerk and one book depository clerk; two custodial clerks; five regular fair-copy clerks; one acting clerk; six regular petition clerks and six acting clerks each; one gate supervisory official, a military appointee; and one dedicated custodian.

sentences.zh: 日曆所

translations.literal: Calendar Office
translations.idiomatic: Calendar Office

sentences.zh: 隸秘書省，以著作郎、著作佐郎掌之。

translations.literal: Subordinate to the Secretariat; managed by the Compiler and Assistant Compilers.
translations.idiomatic: It was subordinate to the Secretariat and managed by the Compiler and Assistant Compilers.

sentences.zh: 以宰執時政記、左右史起居注所書會集修撰為一 代之典。

translations.literal: Using the chief ministers' records of current policy and what the Left and Right Historians entered in the diary notes, it compiled the standard record of an age.
translations.idiomatic: It compiled the standard record of a reign from the chief ministers' policy diaries and the diary notes kept by the Left and Right Historians.

sentences.zh: 舊於門下省置編修院，專掌國史、實錄，修纂日曆。

translations.literal: Formerly a Compilation Bureau was placed in the Chancellery, exclusively managing national history and veritable records and compiling the calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly a Compilation Bureau in the Chancellery exclusively managed national history and veritable records and compiled the court calendar.

sentences.zh: 元豐元年詔：「宣徽院等 供報修注事，自今更不供起居院，直供編修院日曆所。」

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanfeng an edict stated: "Reporting affairs for revision of diary notes from the Palace Council and the like—henceforth they shall not be supplied to the Diary Office but supplied directly to the Calendar Office of the Compilation Bureau."
translations.idiomatic: In 1078 an edict ordered: "Reports for diary revision from the Palace Council and similar offices shall no longer go to the Diary Office but directly to the Compilation Bureau's Calendar Office."

sentences.zh: 四年十一月，廢編修院歸史館 。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year the Compilation Bureau was abolished and returned to the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fourth year the Compilation Bureau was abolished and merged back into the History Office.

sentences.zh: 官制行，屬秘書省國史案。

translations.literal: When the official system was implemented, it belonged to the National History section of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under the reformed official system it belonged to the Secretariat's National History section.

sentences.zh: 六年，詔秘書省長、貳毋得預著作修纂日曆事，進書即擊 銜，以防漏洩，如舊編修院法焉。

translations.literal: In the sixth year an edict ordered that the chief and second of the Secretariat not participate in calendar compilation by the Compilation Bureau; upon presenting books they should punch their seals, to prevent leaks, as under the old Compilation Bureau law.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year an edict barred the Secretariat Director and Vice Director from calendar compilation work; on submitting texts they were to stamp their seals to prevent leaks, as under the old Compilation Bureau rules.

sentences.zh: 八年，詔吏部郎中曾肇、禮部郎中林希兼著作。

translations.literal: In the eighth year an edict ordered Zeng Zhao, Director in the Ministry of Personnel, and Lin Xi, Director in the Ministry of Rites, to hold Compiler posts concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Zeng Zhao of the Ministry of Personnel and Lin Xi of the Ministry of Rites were ordered to serve concurrently as Compilers.

sentences.zh: 職事 官兼職自此始。

translations.literal: Concurrent posts for regular-duty officials began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Concurrent service by regular-duty officials began from this point.

sentences.zh: 元祐五年，移國史案置局，專掌國史、實錄，編修日曆，以國史院為名，隸門下省，更 不隸秘書省。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanyou the National History section was moved to establish a separate bureau, exclusively managing national history and veritable records and compiling the calendar; it was named the National History Office, subordinate to the Chancellery and no longer subordinate to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1090 the National History section was reorganized as a separate bureau—the National History Office—under the Chancellery, exclusively managing national history, veritable records, and the calendar, no longer under the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 紹聖二年，詔日曆還秘書省。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaosheng an edict returned the calendar to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1095 the calendar was returned to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 宣和二年，詔罷在京修書諸局，惟秘書省日 曆所係元豐國史案，除著作郎官專管修纂日曆之事無定員外，其分案編修日曆書庫官吏 ，並依元豐法。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuanhe an edict abolished all capital book-compilation bureaus; only the Secretariat's Calendar Office preserved the Yuanfeng National History section. Except that Compiler posts specifically managing calendar compilation had no fixed quota, the sectional clerks and book-depository officials for compiling the calendar followed the Yuanfeng law.
translations.idiomatic: In 1120 all capital book-compilation bureaus were abolished except the Secretariat's Calendar Office, which preserved the Yuanfeng National History arrangement; Compiler posts for calendar work had no fixed quota, but sectional clerks and book-depository staff followed Yuanfeng rules.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，初修皇帝日曆，詔以修日曆所為名，本省長貳通行修纂。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing the emperor's calendar was first compiled; an edict ordered it named the Office for Compiling the Calendar, with the provincial chief and second conducting compilation jointly.
translations.idiomatic: In 1131 the emperor's calendar was first compiled; the office was named the Office for Compiling the Calendar, with the Secretariat Director and Vice Director jointly overseeing compilation.

sentences.zh: 三 年，詔宰臣提舉，侍從官修撰，十一月，詔以修國史日曆所為名。

translations.literal: In the third year an edict ordered chief ministers to supervise and palace attendees to compile; in the eleventh month an edict named it the Office for Compiling National History and the Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year chief ministers were ordered to supervise and palace attendees to compile; in the eleventh month it was named the Office for Compiling National History and the Calendar.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔以史館為名 。

translations.literal: In the fourth year an edict named it the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year it was renamed the History Office.

sentences.zh: 十年，詔依舊制並歸秘書省國史案，以著作郎、佐修纂，舊史館官罷歸元官。

translations.literal: In the tenth year an edict ordered that by the old system all be merged back into the National History section of the Secretariat, with Compilers and Assistant Compilers compiling; former History Office officials were dismissed and returned to original posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year an edict restored the old arrangement: all work returned to the Secretariat's National History section, with Compilers and Assistant Compilers doing the compilation; former History Office staff returned to their original posts.

sentences.zh: 尋復詔 以國史日曆所為名，續併修神宗、哲宗寶訓。

translations.literal: Soon another edict ordered it named the Office of National History and the Calendar, continuing compilation of the Sacred Instructions of Shenzong and Zhezong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon it was again named the Office of National History and the Calendar, which also compiled the Sacred Instructions of Shenzong and Zhezong.

sentences.zh: 隆興元年，詔編類聖政所併歸日曆所，依 舊宰臣提領，仍令日曆所吏充行遣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longxing an edict merged the Bureau for Compiling the Sacred Governance into the Calendar Office; chief ministers still headed it as before, and Calendar Office clerks were ordered to handle its business.
translations.idiomatic: In 1163 the Bureau for Compiling the Sacred Governance was merged into the Calendar Office; chief ministers still headed it, and Calendar Office clerks handled its routine business.

sentences.zh: 會要所

translations.literal: Compendium Office
translations.idiomatic: Compendium Office

sentences.zh: 以省官通任其事。

translations.literal: Provincial officials jointly undertook the work.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat officials jointly undertook the work.

sentences.zh: 紹興九年，詔秘書省官讎校國朝會要，逐官添給茶湯錢。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Shaoxing an edict ordered Secretariat officials to collate the Song dynasty compendium, and each official received supplementary tea and soup money.
translations.idiomatic: In 1139 Secretariat officials were ordered to collate the Song dynastic compendium, with supplementary tea and soup allowances for each officer.

sentences.zh: 乾道四年， 詔尚書右僕射陳俊卿兼提舉編修國朝會要，每遇提舉官開院過局，就本省道山堂聚呈文 字，提舉諸司官、承受官、主管諸司官，並令國史日曆所官兼。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qiandao an edict ordered Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat Chen Junqing to supervise compilation of the Song dynasty compendium; whenever the supervisor opened the bureau and passed through the office, documents were presented at the Daoshan Hall in this province. Supervisor of all bureaus, receiving official, and executive officials of each bureau were all filled concurrently by officials of the National History and Calendar Office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1168 Right Vice Minister Chen Junqing was ordered to supervise compilation of the Song dynastic compendium; when the supervisor convened the bureau, documents were presented at the Secretariat's Daoshan Hall. Supervisory, receiving, and executive officials were all drawn concurrently from the National History and Calendar Office.

sentences.zh: 五年，令本省再加刪定 ，以續修國朝會要為名。

translations.literal: In the fifth year this province was ordered to undertake further editing, under the name Continued Compilation of the Song Dynasty Compendium.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the Secretariat was ordered to undertake further editing under the title Continued Compilation of the Song Dynastic Compendium.

sentences.zh: 九年，秘書少監陳騤言：「編類建炎以後會要成書，以中興會 要為名。」

translations.literal: In the ninth year Vice Director Chen Kui said: "Compilation of the compendium from the Jianyan period onward is complete; let it be named the Restoration Compendium."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Vice Director Chen Kui reported: "The classified compendium from the Jianyan period onward is complete; let it be titled the Restoration Compendium."

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: Both were approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 其後接續修纂，並隸秘書省。

translations.literal: Thereafter successive compilation was also subordinate to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Subsequent compilations also remained under the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 國史實錄院 提舉國史 監修國史 提舉實錄院 修國史 同修國史 史館修撰、同修撰 實錄院修撰、同修撰 直史館 編修官 檢討官 校勘、檢閱、校正、編校官

translations.literal: National History and Veritable Records Office; Supervisor of National History; Overseer of National History; Supervisor of the Veritable Records Office; Compiler of National History; Associate Compiler of National History; History Office Compiler and Associate Compiler; Veritable Records Office Compiler and Associate Compiler; Direct Attendant of the History Office; Compilation Official; Investigating Official; Collator, Reviewer, Corrector, and Editorial Collator.
translations.idiomatic: National History and Veritable Records Office; Supervisor of National History; Overseer of National History; Supervisor of the Veritable Records Office; Compiler of National History; Associate Compiler of National History; History Office Compiler and Associate Compiler; Veritable Records Office Compiler and Associate Compiler; Direct Attendant of the History Office; Compilation Official; Investigating Official; Collator, Reviewer, Corrector, and Editorial Collator.

sentences.zh: 初，紹興三年，詔置國史院，重修神宗、哲宗實錄，以從官充修撰，續以左僕射呂頤浩 提舉國史，右僕射朱勝非監修國史。

translations.literal: At first, in the third year of Shaoxing, an edict ordered establishment of the National History Office to recompile the Veritable Records of Shenzong and Zhezong; palace attendees served as Compilers. Subsequently Left Chief Councillor Lü Yihao was appointed Supervisor of National History and Right Chief Councillor Zhu Shengfei Overseer of National History.
translations.idiomatic: In 1133 the National History Office was established to recompile the Veritable Records of Shenzong and Zhezong, with palace attendees as compilers; Left Chief Councillor Lü Yihao was appointed Supervisor of National History and Right Chief Councillor Zhu Shengfei Overseer of National History.

sentences.zh: 四年，置直史館及檢討、校勘各一員。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Direct Attendants of the History Office and one each of Investigator and Collator were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year a Direct Attendant of the History Office and one each of Investigator and Collator were established.

sentences.zh: 五年，置修 撰官二員，校勘官無定員。

translations.literal: In the fifth year two Compiler posts were established; Collators had no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year two compiler posts were established; collators had no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 是時，國史、實錄皆寓史館，未有置此廢彼之分。

translations.literal: At the time national history and veritable records were both lodged in the History Office; there was not yet the distinction of establishing one and abolishing another.
translations.idiomatic: At the time national history and veritable records both lodged in the History Office; there was not yet a separate establishment for each.

sentences.zh: 九年，修 徽宗實錄，詔以實錄院為名，仍以宰臣提舉，以從官充修撰、同修撰，餘官充檢討，無 定員。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, compiling the Veritable Records of Huizong, an edict named it the Veritable Records Office; chief ministers still supervised; palace attendees served as Compilers and Associate Compilers; other officials served as Investigators without fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, compiling Huizong's Veritable Records, an edict named the office the Veritable Records Office; chief ministers still supervised; palace attendees served as compilers and associate compilers; other officials served as investigators without fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 明年，以未修正史，詔罷史館官吏併歸實錄院。

translations.literal: The following year, because the standard history had not yet been corrected, an edict abolished History Office clerks and merged them into the Veritable Records Office.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, because the standard history had not yet been revised, History Office staff were abolished and merged into the Veritable Records Office.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，實錄書成，詔修三朝 正史，復置國史院，以宰臣監修，侍從官兼同修，餘官充編修。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, when the veritable records were complete, an edict ordered compilation of the standard histories of three reigns; the National History Office was reestablished, with chief ministers as Overseers, palace attendees as Associate Compilers concurrently, and other officials as Compilation Officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year, when the veritable records were complete, an edict ordered compilation of the standard histories of three reigns; the National History Office was reestablished, with chief ministers as overseers, palace attendees as associate compilers, and other officials as compilation officials.

sentences.zh: 明年，詔國史院以宰臣 提舉置修國史、同修國史共二員。

translations.literal: The following year an edict ordered the National History Office supervised by chief ministers, establishing two posts of Compiler of National History and Associate Compiler of National History.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the National History Office was placed under chief-minister supervision, with two posts established: Compiler of National History and Associate Compiler of National History.

sentences.zh: 編修官二員，又置都大提舉諸司官、承受官、諸司官 各一員。

translations.literal: Two Compilation Officials were established; also one each of Grand Supervisor of Various Offices, Reception Officer, and Various Offices Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Two compilation officials were added, along with one post each for grand supervisor of various offices, reception officer, and various-offices officer.

sentences.zh: 以內侍省官充。

translations.literal: Filled by officials of the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: These posts were filled by Palace Domestic Service officials.

sentences.zh: 隆興元年，以編類聖政所併歸國史院，命起居郎胡銓同修國史 。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longxing, the Institute for Compiling Sagely Governance was merged into the National History Office; Attendant Gentleman for the Court Diary Hu Quan was ordered as Associate Compiler of National History.
translations.idiomatic: In 1163 the Institute for Compiling Sagely Governance was merged into the National History Office, and Hu Quan, Attendant Gentleman for the Court Diary, was appointed associate compiler of national history.

sentences.zh: 二年，參政錢端禮權監修國史；

translations.literal: In the second year, Vice Grand Councillor Qian Duanli served concurrently as Overseer of National History;
translations.idiomatic: In the following year Vice Grand Councillor Qian Duanli served concurrently as overseer of national history;

sentences.zh: 乾道元年，參政虞允文權提舉國史：皆前所未有。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiandao, Vice Grand Councillor Yu Yunwen served concurrently as Supervisor of National History: all without precedent.
translations.idiomatic: in 1165 Vice Grand Councillor Yu Yunwen served concurrently as supervisor of national history—arrangements without precedent in either case.

sentences.zh: 二 年，詔置實錄院，修欽宗實錄，其修撰、檢討官以史院官兼領。

translations.literal: In the second year, an edict established the Veritable Records Office to compile the Veritable Records of Qinzong; its Compiler and Investigator posts were held concurrently by History Office officials.
translations.idiomatic: In 1166 the Veritable Records Office was established to compile Qinzong's veritable records, with compilers and investigators drawn concurrently from the History Office staff.

sentences.zh: 四年，實錄告成，詔修 欽宗正史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when the veritable records were complete, an edict ordered compilation of Qinzong's standard history.
translations.idiomatic: When the veritable records were finished in 1168, an edict ordered compilation of Qinzong's standard history.

sentences.zh: 以右僕射蔣芾提舉四朝國史，詔增置編修官二員，續又增置三員。

translations.literal: Right Chief Councillor Jiang Fu was appointed Supervisor of the National History of Four Reigns; an edict added two Compilation Officials, and subsequently three more were added.
translations.idiomatic: Right Chief Councillor Jiang Fu was appointed supervisor of the national history of four reigns; two compilation officials were added by edict, and three more followed.

sentences.zh: 淳熙三年 ，特命李燾以秘書監權同修國史、權實靈院同修撰。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunxi, Li Tao was specially ordered, while Superintendent of the Secretariat, to serve concurrently as Associate Compiler of National History and concurrently as Associate Compiler of the Veritable Records Office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1176 Li Tao was specially appointed, while serving as superintendent of the Secretariat, as concurrent associate compiler of national history and concurrent associate compiler of the Veritable Records Office.

sentences.zh: 四年，罷實錄院，專置史院。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the Veritable Records Office was abolished and only the History Office was established.
translations.idiomatic: In 1177 the Veritable Records Office was abolished and a dedicated History Office alone was retained.

sentences.zh: 十五 年，四朝國史成書，詔罷史院，復開實錄院修高宗實錄。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, when the National History of Four Reigns was completed, an edict abolished the History Office and reopened the Veritable Records Office to compile the Veritable Records of Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: When the national history of four reigns was completed in 1188, the History Office was abolished and the Veritable Records Office reopened to compile Gaozong's veritable records.

sentences.zh: 慶元元年，開實錄院修纂孝宗 實錄。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qingyuan, the Veritable Records Office was opened to compile the Veritable Records of Xiaozong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1195 the Veritable Records Office was opened to compile Xiaozong's veritable records.

sentences.zh: 六年，詔實錄院同修撰以四員、檢討官以六員為額。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, an edict fixed the quota of Associate Compilers of the Veritable Records Office at four and Investigators at six.
translations.idiomatic: In 1200 the Veritable Records Office was capped at four associate compilers and six investigators.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰元年，開實錄院修纂光 宗實錄。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiatai, the Veritable Records Office was opened to compile the Veritable Records of Guangzong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1201 the Veritable Records Office was opened to compile Guangzong's veritable records.

sentences.zh: 二年，復開國史院，自是國史與實錄院並置矣。

translations.literal: In the second year, the National History Office was reopened; from then on the National History Office and Veritable Records Office existed side by side.
translations.idiomatic: In 1202 the National History Office was reopened, and thereafter national history and veritable records were maintained in separate offices.

sentences.zh: 實錄院吏兼行國史院事，點檢 文字一人，書庫官八人，楷書四人。

translations.literal: Veritable Records Office clerks also handled National History Office affairs; there was one Text Inspector, eight Archive Clerks, and four Copyists.
translations.idiomatic: Veritable Records Office clerks also handled National History Office business, with one text inspector, eight archive clerks, and four copyists.

sentences.zh: 太史局

translations.literal: Imperial Astronomical Bureau
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Astronomical Bureau

sentences.zh: 掌測驗天文，考定曆法。

translations.literal: It managed observation and measurement of the heavens and determination of the calendar.
translations.idiomatic: It observed and measured celestial phenomena and fixed the calendar.

sentences.zh: 凡日月、星辰、風雲、氣候、祥眚之事，日具所佔以聞。

translations.literal: For all matters of sun, moon, stars, winds, clouds, weather, and auspicious or inauspicious signs, it daily recorded divinations and reported them.
translations.idiomatic: For the sun, moon, stars, winds, clouds, weather, and omens of fortune or calamity, it recorded daily prognostications and reported them to court.

sentences.zh: 歲頒 曆於天下，則預造進呈。

translations.literal: When the calendar was issued yearly to the empire, it prepared them in advance and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: When the annual calendar was issued empire-wide, it prepared the editions in advance and presented them for approval.

sentences.zh: 祭祀、冠昏及大典禮，則選所用日。

translations.literal: For sacrifices, capping and marriage, and great ceremonies, it selected the days to be used.
translations.idiomatic: For sacrifices, capping and marriage ceremonies, and major state rituals, it selected the auspicious days.

sentences.zh: 其官有令，有正，有春官 、夏官、中官、秋官、冬官正，有丞，有直長，有靈臺郎，有保章正。

translations.literal: Its offices included a Director, a Chief Director, Spring, Summer, Center, Autumn, and Winter Chief Directors, a Vice Director, Section Chiefs, Observatory Clerks, and Keepers of Auspicious Portents.
translations.idiomatic: Its posts comprised a director, a chief director, spring, summer, center, autumn, and winter chief directors, a vice director, section chiefs, observatory clerks, and keepers of auspicious portents.

sentences.zh: 其判局及同判， 則選五官正以上業優考深者充。

translations.literal: Its Bureau Chief and Associate Bureau Chief were filled by selecting those among Chief Directors of the Five Offices and above who excelled in their specialty and had deep examination records.
translations.idiomatic: Its bureau chief and associate bureau chief were chosen from chief directors of the five offices and above who had distinguished records of service and examination.

sentences.zh: 保章正五年、直長至令十年一遷，惟靈臺郎試中乃遷， 而挈壺正無遷法。

translations.literal: Keepers of Auspicious Portents were promoted every five years; Section Chiefs through Director every ten years; only Observatory Clerks were promoted after passing examination; the Water Clock Keeper had no promotion rule.
translations.idiomatic: Keepers of auspicious portents advanced every five years and section chiefs through directors every ten; observatory clerks advanced only after passing examination, while the water-clock keeper had no regular promotion schedule.

sentences.zh: 其別局有天文院、測驗渾儀刻漏所，掌渾儀臺晝夜測驗辰象。
