translations.idiomatic: The minister managed sacrifices, court assemblies, banquets, village libations, food, drink, and delicacies, maintaining stores and carefully governing disbursement and receipt; the vice minister was second in rank; the vice director assisted.

sentences.zh: 凡祭祀，共五齊、三酒、牲牢、鬱鬯及尊彝、籩豆、簠簋、鼎俎、鉶 登之實，前期飭有司辦具牲鑊，視滌濯，奉牲則告充告各，共其明水火焉。

translations.literal: For all sacrifices, they jointly supplied the five ritual preparations, three wines, sacrificial victims, aromatic wine, and the filling of ritual vessels including zun and yi, baskets and stands, grain vessels, tripods and trays, and meat stands; beforehand ordering relevant offices to prepare cauldrons and victims, inspecting washing, when presenting victims reporting fullness to each, jointly supplying clear water and fire.
translations.idiomatic: For all sacrifices they jointly supplied the five graded preparations, three wines, sacrificial victims, aromatic wine, and the filling of ritual vessels—zun and yi, baskets and stands, grain vessels, tripods and trays, and meat stands; beforehand they ordered the relevant offices to prepare cauldrons and victims, inspected washing, and when presenting victims reported fullness to each, jointly supplying clear water and fire.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，進胙 於天子而頒於百執事之人。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, sacrificial meat was presented to the Son of Heaven and distributed to the hundred officers.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete, sacrificial meat was presented to the Son of Heaven and distributed to the hundred officers.

sentences.zh: 分案五，置吏十。

translations.literal: Five sections, ten clerks.
translations.idiomatic: There were five sections and ten clerks.

sentences.zh: 元祐三年，詔長貳互置。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanyou, an edict directed the chief and deputy to serve alternately.
translations.idiomatic: In 1088 an edict directed the chief and deputy ministers to serve alternately.

sentences.zh: 政和六年二月， 監察御史王桓奏：「祭祀牢醴之具掌於光祿，而寺官未嘗臨視，請大祠以長貳、朔祭及 中祠以丞簿監視宰割，禮畢頒胙，有故及小祠，聽以其屬攝。」

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year of Zhenghe, investigating censor Wang Huan memorialized: "Sacrificial victims and libations are in charge of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, yet court officials have never personally inspected; for great sacrifices let the chief and deputy, for new-moon sacrifices and medium sacrifices let vice director and registrar supervise slaughter; when the rite is complete distribute sacrificial meat; for urgency and small sacrifices, their subordinates may act in proxy."
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of 1116 investigating censor Wang Huan memorialized, "Sacrificial victims and libations are in the charge of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, yet court officials have never personally inspected them. For great sacrifices let the chief and deputy ministers, for new-moon and medium sacrifices let the vice director and registrar supervise slaughter; when the rite is complete distribute sacrificial meat; in cases of urgency and for small sacrifices, subordinates may act in proxy."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was adopted.

sentences.zh: 舊置判寺事一人 ，以朝官以上充。

translations.literal: Formerly one supervisor of court affairs was established, filled by court officials and above.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly one supervisor of court affairs was established, filled by court officials and above.

sentences.zh: 光祿卿、少，皆為寄祿。

translations.literal: The minister and vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments were all salary-conferring sinecures.
translations.idiomatic: The minister and vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments were all salary-conferring sinecures.

sentences.zh: 元豐制行，始歸本寺。

translations.literal: When the Yuanfeng system took effect, [duties] were first returned to this court.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuanfeng reforms took effect, full jurisdiction returned to the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 中興後，廢併入禮部 。

translations.literal: After the restoration, [the court] was abolished and merged into the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration it was abolished and merged into the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 太官令

translations.literal: Director of the Grand Provisioner
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Grand Provisioner

sentences.zh: 掌膳羞割烹之事。

translations.literal: He managed delicacies, cutting, and cooking.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw delicacies, cutting, and cooking.

sentences.zh: 凡供進膳羞，則辨其名物，而視食之宜，謹其水火之齊。

translations.literal: For all food presented, he identified name and kind, observed what was suitable to eat, and carefully regulated fire and water proportions.
translations.idiomatic: For all food presented at court, he identified each item by name, judged what was suitable to eat, and carefully regulated cooking times and heat.

sentences.zh: 祭祀共明水 、明火，割牲取毛血牲體，以為鼎俎之實。

translations.literal: At sacrifices he jointly supplied clear water and bright fire, cut victims and took hair, blood, and victim flesh as filling for tripods and trays.
translations.idiomatic: At sacrifices he jointly supplied clear water and sacred fire, cut the victims, took hair, blood, and flesh, and prepared the fillings for tripods and trays.

sentences.zh: 朝會宴享，則供其酒膳。

translations.literal: At court assemblies and banquets, he supplied wine and meals.
translations.idiomatic: At court assemblies and banquets he supplied wine and meals.

sentences.zh: 凡給賜，視其品秩 而為之等。

translations.literal: For all grants and gifts, according to rank he made grades.
translations.idiomatic: For all grants and gifts, he set grades according to official rank.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，罷太官令。

translations.literal: In early Yuanyou, the Director of the Grand Provisioner was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In 1086 the post of Director of the Grand Provisioner was abolished.

sentences.zh: 二年復置。

translations.literal: In the second year [the post] was restored.
translations.idiomatic: It was restored in 1087.

sentences.zh: （崇寧三年，置尚食局，太官令惟掌祠事。）〉

translations.literal: (In the third year of Chongning, the Bureau of Imperial Food was established; the Director of the Grand Provisioner managed only sacrificial affairs.)
translations.idiomatic: (In 1104 the Bureau of Imperial Food was established; the Director of the Grand Provisioner managed only sacrificial affairs.)

sentences.zh: 法酒庫 內酒坊

translations.literal: Standard Wine Storehouse; Inner Wine Brewery
translations.idiomatic: Standard Wine Storehouse; Inner Wine Brewery

sentences.zh: 掌以式法授酒材，視其厚薄之齊，而謹其出納之政。

translations.literal: They managed dispensing brewing materials by statutory method, observed thickness proportions, and carefully governed disbursement and receipt.
translations.idiomatic: They dispensed brewing materials by statutory formula, regulated thickness and strength, and carefully governed disbursement and receipt.

sentences.zh: 若造酒以待供進及祭祀，給賜，則 法酒庫掌之；

translations.literal: If brewing wine to await court presentation, sacrifices, and grants, the Standard Wine Storehouse managed it;
translations.idiomatic: Wine brewed for court presentation, sacrifices, and grants was managed by the Standard Wine Storehouse;

sentences.zh: 凡祭祀，供五齊三酒，以實尊罍。

translations.literal: For all sacrifices, they supplied the five preparations and three wines to fill zun and lei vessels.
translations.idiomatic: For all sacrifices they supplied the five graded preparations and three wines to fill the ritual zun and lei vessels.

sentences.zh: 內酒坊惟造酒，以待餘用。

translations.literal: The Inner Wine Brewery only brewed wine for remaining uses.
translations.idiomatic: The Inner Wine Brewery brewed only for other uses.

sentences.zh: 太官物料庫 掌預備膳食薦羞之物，以供太官之用，辨其名數而會其出入。

translations.literal: The Grand Provisioner Materials Storehouse prepared food and delicacies for the Grand Provisioner's use, identified kinds and numbers, and tallied disbursement and receipt.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Provisioner Materials Storehouse prepared meals and delicacies for the Grand Provisioner's use, identified each item by kind and number, and tallied disbursements and receipts.

sentences.zh: 翰林司 掌供果實及茶茗湯藥。

translations.literal: The Hanlin Provisioners Office supplied fruits, tea, broths, and medicines.
translations.idiomatic: The Hanlin Provisioners Office supplied fruits, tea, broths, and medicines.

sentences.zh: 牛羊司、牛羊供應所 掌供大中小祀之牲牷及太官宴享膳羞之用。

translations.literal: The Cattle and Sheep Office and Cattle and Sheep Supply Depot supplied sacrificial oxen for great, medium, and small sacrifices and delicacies for the Grand Provisioner's banquets.
translations.idiomatic: The Cattle and Sheep Office and the Cattle and Sheep Supply Depot supplied sacrificial oxen for great, medium, and small sacrifices and delicacies for the Grand Provisioner's banquets.

sentences.zh: 乳酪院 掌供造酥酪。

translations.literal: The Dairy Court supplied butter and cheese.
translations.idiomatic: The Dairy Court supplied butter and cheese.

sentences.zh: 油醋庫 掌供油及鹽胾。

translations.literal: The Oil and Vinegar Storehouse supplied oil and pickled meats.
translations.idiomatic: The Oil and Vinegar Storehouse supplied oil and pickled meats.

sentences.zh: 外物料庫 掌收儲米、鹽、雜物以待膳食之須。

translations.literal: The External Materials Storehouse stored rice, salt, and miscellaneous goods for meal needs.
translations.idiomatic: The External Materials Storehouse stored rice, salt, and miscellaneous goods against the needs of the kitchen.

sentences.zh: 凡百司頒給者取具焉。

translations.literal: All hundred offices taking grants obtained supplies there.
translations.idiomatic: All agencies drawing allotments obtained their supplies there.

sentences.zh: 衛尉寺 卿 少卿 丞

translations.literal: Court of the Imperial Insignia: Minister, Vice Minister, Vice Director
translations.idiomatic: Court of the Imperial Insignia: minister, vice minister, vice director

sentences.zh: 主簿各一人。

translations.literal: Registrar, one each.
translations.idiomatic: Each office had one registrar.

sentences.zh: 卿掌儀衛兵械、甲胃之政令，少卿為之貳，丞參領之。

translations.literal: The minister managed ceremonial guard weapons and armor regulations; the vice minister was his deputy; the vice director assisted.
translations.idiomatic: The minister managed regulations for ceremonial guard weapons and armor; the vice minister was second in rank; the vice director assisted.

sentences.zh: 凡內外作坊輸納兵 器，則辨其名數、驗其良窳以歸於武庫，不如式者罰之。

translations.literal: When inner and outer workshops delivered weapons, [officials] identified names and numbers, inspected quality for return to the armory, and penalized those not meeting specifications.
translations.idiomatic: When inner and outer workshops delivered weapons, officials identified each item, inspected quality before entry into the armory, and penalized goods that failed to meet specifications.

sentences.zh: 時其曝涼而封籍其數，若進御 及頒給，則按籍而出之。

translations.literal: They timed airing and drying and sealed registers of quantities; for imperial use and grants, items were issued according to the register.
translations.idiomatic: They scheduled airing and drying, sealed registers of quantities, and for imperial use and grants issued items strictly according to the register.

sentences.zh: 每季委官檢視，歲終上計帳於兵部。

translations.literal: Each quarter they delegated officials to inspect; at year's end they submitted accounts to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Each quarter they delegated officials to inspect stores; at year's end they submitted accounts to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 掌凡幄帟之事，大禮設帷 宮，張大次、小次，陳鹵簿儀仗。

translations.literal: They managed all awning and curtain matters; for great rites they set palatial tents, raised great and small canopies, and arrayed insignia guard and ceremonial arms.
translations.idiomatic: They managed all awnings and curtains; for great rites they erected the palatial tent, raised the great and small canopies, and arrayed the insignia guard and ceremonial arms.

sentences.zh: 長貳晝夜巡徼，察其不如儀者，押仗官則前期稟差。

translations.literal: The chief and deputy patrolled day and night, observing those not observing protocol; escort officers reported assignments beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: The chief and deputy ministers patrolled day and night and observed breaches of protocol; escort officers reported their assignments in advance.

sentences.zh: 凡仗衛，供羽儀、節鉞、金鼓、棨戟，朝宴亦如之。

translations.literal: For guard of honor they supplied regalia, batons of authority, gongs and drums, and halberds; the same at court banquets.
translations.idiomatic: For the guard of honor they supplied regalia, batons of authority, gongs and drums, and halberds; court banquets were supplied likewise.

sentences.zh: 宴享賓客，供幕帟、茵席，視其敝 者移少府、軍器監修焉。

translations.literal: For banquets entertaining guests they supplied curtains and mats; worn ones were sent to the Directorate of the Palace Stores and the Directorate of Armaments for repair.
translations.idiomatic: For banquets entertaining guests they supplied curtains and mats; worn items were sent to the Directorate of the Palace Stores and the Directorate of Armaments for repair.

sentences.zh: 舊制，判寺事一人，以郎官以上充。

translations.literal: Under the old system, one supervisor of court affairs was established, filled by bureau directors and above.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system one supervisor of court affairs was appointed, filled by a bureau director or higher.

sentences.zh: 凡武庫、武器歸內庫，守 宮歸儀鸞司，本寺無所掌。

translations.literal: The armory and weapons belonged to the inner storehouse; palace guard belonged to the Ceremonial Parasols Office; this court had nothing in charge.
translations.idiomatic: The armory and weapons belonged to the inner storehouse, palace guard to the Ceremonial Parasols Office, and this court had no jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 元豐官制行，始歸本寺。

translations.literal: When the Yuanfeng official system took effect, [duties] were first returned to this court.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuanfeng official system took effect, full jurisdiction returned to the Court of the Imperial Insignia.

sentences.zh: 分案四，置吏十。

translations.literal: Four sections, ten clerks.
translations.idiomatic: There were four sections and ten clerks.

sentences.zh: 元祐三年、詔長 貳互置。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanyou, an edict directed the chief and deputy to serve alternately.
translations.idiomatic: In 1088 an edict directed the chief and deputy ministers to serve alternately.

sentences.zh: 所隸官司十有三：內弓箭庫、南外庫、軍器弓槍庫、軍器弩劍箭庫，掌藏兵杖 、器械、甲胃，以備軍國之用。

translations.literal: Subordinate offices numbered thirteen: the Inner Bow Storehouse, South Outer Storehouse, Armaments Bow and Spear Storehouse, and Armaments Crossbow, Sword, and Arrow Storehouse, which stored weapons, implements, and armor for state and army use.
translations.idiomatic: It had thirteen subordinate offices: the Inner Bow Storehouse, South Outer Storehouse, Armaments Bow and Spear Storehouse, and Armaments Crossbow, Sword, and Arrow Storehouse, which stored weapons, implements, and armor for state and army use.

sentences.zh: 儀鸞司，掌供幕帟供帳之事。

translations.literal: The Ceremonial Parasols Office managed supplying curtains and camp furnishings.
translations.idiomatic: The Ceremonial Parasols Office supplied curtains and camp furnishings.

sentences.zh: 軍器什物庫、宣德樓什物 庫，掌收貯什物，給用則按籍而頒之。

translations.literal: The Armaments Sundries Storehouse and Xuande Tower Sundries Storehouse stored sundries and issued them according to the register when needed.
translations.idiomatic: The Armaments Sundries Storehouse and the Xuande Tower Sundries Storehouse stored sundries and issued them according to the register when needed.

sentences.zh: 左右金吾街司、左右金吾仗司、六軍儀仗司，掌 清道、徼巡、排列，奉引儀仗以肅禁衛。

translations.literal: The Left and Right Golden Guard Street Offices, Left and Right Golden Guard Escort Offices, and Six Armies Ceremonial Guard Office cleared the roads, patrolled, arrayed ranks, and led ceremonial arms to maintain palace security.
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Golden Guard Street Offices, Left and Right Golden Guard Escort Offices, and Six Armies Ceremonial Guard Office cleared the roads, patrolled, arrayed ranks, and led the ceremonial guard to maintain palace security.

sentences.zh: 凡儀物以時修飭，選募人兵而校其遷補之事。

translations.literal: They maintained regalia in season, selected and recruited men-at-arms, and regulated their promotion and replacement.
translations.idiomatic: They maintained regalia on schedule, recruited guardsmen, and regulated their promotion and replacement.

sentences.zh: 中興後，衛尉寺廢，併入工部。

translations.literal: After the restoration, the Court of the Imperial Insignia was abolished and merged into the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration the Court of the Imperial Insignia was abolished and merged into the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 太僕寺 卿 少卿 丞

translations.literal: Court of the Imperial Stud: Minister, Vice Minister, Vice Director
translations.idiomatic: Court of the Imperial Stud: minister, vice minister, vice director

sentences.zh: 主簿各一人。

translations.literal: Registrar, one each.
translations.idiomatic: Each office had one registrar.

sentences.zh: 卿掌車輅、廄牧之令，少卿為之貳，丞參領之。

translations.literal: The minister managed regulations for chariots and stud pastures; the vice minister was his deputy; the vice director assisted.
translations.idiomatic: The minister managed regulations for chariots and stud pastures; the vice minister was second in rank; the vice director assisted.

sentences.zh: 國有大禮，供其輦輅、屬 車，前期戒有司教閱象馬。

translations.literal: When the state held a great rite, they supplied imperial chariots and attendant vehicles; beforehand they ordered the relevant offices to drill elephants and horses.
translations.idiomatic: When the state held a great rite, they supplied imperial chariots and attendant vehicles; beforehand they ordered the relevant offices to drill elephants and horses.

sentences.zh: 凡儀仗既陳，則巡視其行列。

translations.literal: Once the ceremonial guard was arrayed, they inspected its ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Once the ceremonial guard was arrayed, they inspected its ranks.

sentences.zh: 后妃、親王、公主、執政官應 給車乘者，視品秩而頒之。

translations.literal: For empresses, imperial princes, princesses, and chief ministers entitled to carriages, allotments were made according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: For empresses, imperial princes, princesses, and chief ministers entitled to carriages, allotments were made according to rank.

sentences.zh: 總國之馬政，籍京都坊監、畿甸牧地畜馬之數，謹其飼養， 察其治療，考蕃息損耗之實，而定其賞罰焉，死則斂其騣尾、筋革入於官府。

translations.literal: They oversaw the nation's horse policy, registered numbers of horses kept at capital studs and pastures in the capital region, carefully supervised feeding, inspected treatment, assessed gains and losses in breeding, and fixed rewards and punishments; when horses died they collected mane, tail, sinew, and hide for the government.
translations.idiomatic: They oversaw national horse policy, registered horses kept at capital studs and pastures in the capital region, supervised feeding and treatment, assessed breeding gains and losses, and fixed rewards and punishments; when horses died they collected mane, tail, sinew, and hide for the government.

sentences.zh: 凡閱馬， 差次其高下，應給賜則如格。

translations.literal: For all horse inspections they graded quality high and low; grants followed the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: At horse inspections they graded quality; grants followed the regulations.

sentences.zh: 歲終鉤覆帳籍，以上駕部。

translations.literal: At year's end they audited registers and submitted them to the Carriage Office.
translations.idiomatic: At year's end they audited the registers and submitted them to the Carriage Office.

sentences.zh: 若有事於南北郊，侍中請降輿 升輅，則卿授綏。

translations.literal: If rites were held at the southern and northern suburban altars and the attendant-in-chief requested to descend the carriage and mount the chariot, the minister presented the handhold.
translations.idiomatic: When rites were held at the southern and northern suburban altars and the attendant-in-chief asked to descend the carriage and mount the chariot, the minister presented the handhold.

sentences.zh: 舊置判寺事一人。

translations.literal: Formerly one supervisor of court affairs was established.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly one supervisor of court affairs was appointed.

sentences.zh: 以朝官以上充。

translations.literal: Filled by court officials and above.
translations.idiomatic: The post was filled by a court official or higher.

sentences.zh: 凡邦國廄牧、車輿之政令，分隸群 牧司、騏驥院諸坊監，本寺但掌天子五輅、屬車，后妃、王公車輅，給大中小祀羊。

translations.literal: Regulations for national studs and chariots were divided among the Herd Office and the Fine Steeds courtyards and various studs; this court only managed the Son of Heaven's five chariots and attendant vehicles, chariots for consorts and princes, and sheep for great, medium, and small sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: National stud and chariot regulations were divided among the Herd Office and the Fine Steeds courtyards and various studs; this court managed only the Son of Heaven's five chariots and attendant vehicles, chariots for consorts and princes, and sheep for great, medium, and small sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 元 豐官制行，始歸本寺。

translations.literal: When the Yuanfeng official system took effect, [duties] were first returned to this court.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuanfeng official system took effect, full jurisdiction returned to the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 分案五，置吏十有八，總局十有二。

translations.literal: Five sections, eighteen clerks, twelve supervising offices.
translations.idiomatic: There were five sections, eighteen clerks, and twelve supervising offices.

sentences.zh: 元祐二年，詔外監事，令本 寺依群牧司舊法施行；

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanyou, an edict on external stud affairs directed this court to implement them according to the Herd Office's former methods;
translations.idiomatic: In 1087 an edict on external stud affairs directed this court to implement them according to the Herd Office's former methods;

sentences.zh: 應內外馬事專隸太僕，直達樞密院，更不經尚書省及駕部。

translations.literal: All inner and outer horse affairs were placed solely under the Imperial Stud, reporting directly to the Bureau of Military Affairs and no longer passing through the Secretariat or the Carriage Office.
translations.idiomatic: All horse affairs, inner and outer, were placed solely under the Court of the Imperial Stud, reporting directly to the Bureau of Military Affairs and no longer passing through the Secretariat or the Carriage Office.

sentences.zh: 三年 ，詔省主簿一員。

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict cut one registrar post.
translations.idiomatic: In 1088 an edict cut one registrar post.

sentences.zh: 崇寧二年，詔太僕寺依舊制不治外事，歸尚書駕部；

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongning, an edict directed the Court of the Imperial Stud, per the old system, not to manage external affairs and to return them to the Secretariat's Carriage Office;
translations.idiomatic: In 1103 an edict directed the Court of the Imperial Stud, per the old system, not to manage external affairs and to return them to the Secretariat's Carriage Office;

sentences.zh: 應馬事，上樞密 院所隸官司。

translations.literal: Horse affairs were referred to the offices subordinate to the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Horse affairs were referred to the offices subordinate to the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 車輅院 掌乘輿、法物，凡大駕、法駕、小駕供輦輅及奉引屬車，辨其名數與陳列先後之序。

translations.literal: The Chariot Courtyard managed imperial carriages and regalia; for great, legal, and small escorts it supplied chariots and attendant vehicles and distinguished their names, numbers, and order of array.
translations.idiomatic: The Chariot Courtyard managed imperial carriages and regalia; for the great, legal, and small escorts it supplied chariots and attendant vehicles and set their names, numbers, and order of array.

sentences.zh: 左、右騏驥院 左、右天駟監 掌國馬，別其駑良，以待軍國之用。

translations.literal: The Left and Right Fine Steeds courtyards and Left and Right Heavenly Horse studs managed national horses, separating draft from fine for state and army use.
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Fine Steeds courtyards and the Left and Right Heavenly Horse studs managed national horses, separating draft from fine stock for state and army use.

sentences.zh: 鞍轡庫 應奉御馬鞍勒，及以韉轡給賜臣下。

translations.literal: The Saddlery Storehouse supplied imperial horse saddles and bridles and granted bridles and tack to officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Saddlery Storehouse supplied imperial horse saddles and bridles and granted tack to officials.

sentences.zh: 養象所 掌調御馴象。

translations.literal: The Elephant Training Office managed training and taming elephants.
translations.idiomatic: The Elephant Training Office trained and tamed elephants.

sentences.zh: 駝坊 車營致遠務 掌分養雜畜，以供負載般運。

translations.literal: The Camel Yard and Transport Service Yard separately raised miscellaneous pack animals for carrying loads and transport.
translations.idiomatic: The Camel Yard and the Transport Service Yard separately raised pack animals for carrying loads and transport.

sentences.zh: 牧養上下監

translations.literal: Upper and Lower Pasturage studs
translations.idiomatic: Upper and Lower Pasturage studs

sentences.zh: 掌治療病馬及申駒數，有耗失則送皮剝所。

translations.literal: They treated sick horses and reported foal counts; losses were sent to the hide-processing office.
translations.idiomatic: They treated sick horses and reported foal counts; losses were sent to the hide-processing office.

sentences.zh: 元豐末，廢畿內牧馬監。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuanfeng era, horse studs within the capital region were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Yuanfeng era, horse studs within the capital region were abolished.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，置左、右 天廄坊，聽民間承佃牧地。

translations.literal: In early Yuanyou, the Left and Right Heavenly Stud courtyards were established, allowing civilians to lease pasture land.
translations.idiomatic: In 1086 the Left and Right Heavenly Stud courtyards were established, allowing civilians to lease pasture land.

sentences.zh: 紹聖元年，依元豐法置孳生監。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaosheng, breeding studs were established according to Yuanfeng law.
translations.idiomatic: In 1094 breeding studs were established according to Yuanfeng law.

sentences.zh: 中興後，廢太僕寺，併入兵部。

translations.literal: After the restoration, the Court of the Imperial Stud was abolished and merged into the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration the Court of the Imperial Stud was abolished and merged into the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 群牧司

translations.literal: Herd Office
translations.idiomatic: Herd Office

sentences.zh: 制置使一人，景德四年置，以樞密使、副為之。

translations.literal: One commissioner-in-chief, established in the fourth year of Jingde, filled by the censor-in-chief and vice.
translations.idiomatic: One commissioner-in-chief was established in 1007, filled by the censor-in-chief and vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 至道三年，罷而復置。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhidao it was abolished and then restored.
translations.idiomatic: In 997 it was abolished and then restored.

sentences.zh: 使一人，咸平三 年置，以兩省以上官充；

translations.literal: One director, established in the third year of Xianping, filled by officials of the two departments and above;
translations.idiomatic: One director was established in 1000, filled by an official of the two departments or higher;

sentences.zh: 副便一人，以閤門以上及內侍都知充。

translations.literal: One deputy commissioner, filled by the Gate office and above and by directors of the inner service.
translations.idiomatic: One deputy commissioner was filled from the Gate office and above and from directors of the inner service.

sentences.zh: 都監二人，以諸司使以 上充。

translations.literal: Two chief inspectors, filled by commissioners of the various offices and above.
translations.idiomatic: Two chief inspectors were filled by commissioners of the various offices and above.

sentences.zh: 判官二人，以京朝官充。

translations.literal: Two reviewing officers, filled by capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: Two reviewing officers were filled by capital officials.

sentences.zh: 掌內外廄牧之事，周知國馬之政，而察其登耗焉。

translations.literal: They managed inner and outer stud affairs, were thoroughly informed of national horse policy, and observed gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: They managed inner and outer stud affairs, were thoroughly informed of national horse policy, and observed gains and losses.

sentences.zh: 凡受 宣詔、文牒，則以時下於院、監。

translations.literal: Whenever they received imperial edicts and documents, they timely transmitted them to the courtyards and studs.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they received imperial edicts and documents, they transmitted them in timely fashion to the courtyards and studs.

sentences.zh: 大事則制置使同簽署，小事則專遣其副使，都監多不 備置，判官、都監每歲更出諸州巡坊監，點印國馬之蕃息者。

translations.literal: Great affairs were co-signed by the commissioner-in-chief; small affairs were handled solely by the deputy; chief inspectors were often not fully staffed; reviewing officers and chief inspectors each year rotated through the provinces inspecting the courtyards and studs and checking seals on national horse breeding.
translations.idiomatic: Great affairs were co-signed by the commissioner-in-chief; small affairs were handled by the deputy alone; chief inspectors were often not fully staffed; each year reviewing officers and chief inspectors rotated through the provinces inspecting studs and checking seals on national horse breeding.

sentences.zh: 又有左、右廂提點，隸本 司。

translations.literal: There were also left and right wing intendant-supervisors subordinate to this office.
translations.idiomatic: There were also left and right wing intendant-supervisors subordinate to this office.

sentences.zh: 都勾押官一人，勾押官一人，押司官一人。

translations.literal: One chief clerk, one clerk, and one document clerk.
translations.idiomatic: There was one chief clerk, one clerk, and one document clerk.

sentences.zh: 鞍轡庫 使 副使

translations.literal: Saddlery Storehouse: Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner
translations.idiomatic: Saddlery Storehouse: commissioner, deputy commissioner

sentences.zh: 監官二人，以諸司副使及三班使臣、內侍充。

translations.literal: Two superintendents, filled by deputy commissioners, third-rank envoys, and inner attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Two superintendents were filled by deputy commissioners, third-rank envoys, and inner attendants.

sentences.zh: 掌御馬金玉鞍勒，及給賜王公、群臣、外 國使并國信韉轡之名物。

translations.literal: They managed gold and jade saddles and bridles for imperial horses and granted named items of bridles and tack to princes, ministers, foreign envoys, and state-credentialed missions.
translations.idiomatic: They managed gold and jade saddles and bridles for imperial horses and granted tack to princes, ministers, foreign envoys, and state-credentialed missions.

sentences.zh: 勾管一人，典五人，掌庫十四人。

translations.literal: One overseer, five clerks, fourteen storehouse keepers.
translations.idiomatic: There was one overseer, five clerks, and fourteen storehouse keepers.
